title: Zero-Knowledge PCPs of Quasilinear Size via Locally Simulatable Sheaf Codes
authors: Tom Gur, Nicholas Spooner, and Hadas Zeilberger
abstract: We show that for every polynomial $T,b \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, there exist an $O(1)$-query probabilistically checkable proof (PCP) for $\operatorname{NTIME}(T)$ of length $\widetilde{O}\bigl(T(n)+b(n)^2\bigr)$, which is $b(n)$-query perfect zero knowledge. This strictly improves on the polynomial-length zero-knowledge PCPs of Gur, O'Connor, and Spooner (STOC 2024; STOC 2025). Our construction builds on the PCPs of Ben-Sasson and Sudan (SICOMP 2008) and Dinur (JACM 2007). We prove the zero-knowledge property of our PCPs via the new machinery of locally simulatable sheaf codes.

1    Introduction
A probabilistically-checkable proof (PCP) is a proof that can be efficiently verified by querying only a
few locations chosen at random. PCPs are a central object in complexity theory, with deep connections
to cryptography, coding theory and hardness of approximation. In this work we continue the study of
zero-knowledge PCPs [KPT97] (ZKPCPs), which combine efficient verification with a strong privacy
property, namely: any view of the PCP of bounded size should not reveal any information beyond the
truth of the claim.
    In recent work, Gur, O’Connor and Spooner [GOS24; GOS25] showed the existence of zero knowledge
PCPs with parameters matching the original PCP theorem [AS98; ALMSS98]. That is, they showed that
for any query bound b : N → N, there exist an O(1)-query PCPs NP with proof length poly(n, b), such
that the distribution of any local view of size at most b(n) can be perfectly and efficiently simulated.
    Over the decades that followed the original proof of the PCP theorem, much work has been done
to reduce the length of the PCP proof, while maintaining constant query complexity. The current
state-of-the-art of (non-ZK) PCPs [BS08; Din07] achieves quasi-linear proof length, i.e., n · polylog(n).
    In this work we show that there exist ZKPCPs with comparable proof length to the best known non-ZK
PCPs. Our main result is the following.
Theorem 1.1 (informally stated; see Theorem 8.2). For every polynomial
                                                                      T, b : N → N, there exist
O(1)-query ZKPCPs for NTIME(T ) of length O  e T (n) + b(n)2 , which are b(n)-query perfect zero
knowledge.
    Our construction is based on the short PCP of [BS08]. Underlying that construction is a PCP of
proximity (PCPP) for Reed–Solomon codes. Our key technical contribution is to modify this PCPP to
achieve zero knowledge properties and analyse it via a new object we introduce called locally simulatable
sheaf codes. In addition to matching the proof length of the shortest non-ZK PCP constructions, this is
the first construction of a ZKPCP in which the proofplength does not grow multiplicatively in the query
bound; i.e., we obtain zero knowledge up to b(n) ≈ T (n) essentially “for free”, in an asymptotic sense.

Concurrent work
Independently and concurrently to this work, Bafna and Vyas [BV26] obtained constructions of similar
but incomparable objects, which they refer to as “private PCPs”. Unlike ZKPCPs, private PCPs do not
require efficient simulation; on the other hand, the privacy guarantee for private PCPs should also hold in
some sense in the “no” case, whereas ZKPCPs provide a privacy guarantee only in the “yes” case.

Organization of the Paper
The rest of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 3, we lay the ground work by defining concepts
related to sheaf codes. Next, in Section 4, we describe the properties needed for a sheaf code to be testable,
and construct a simple codeword test. After that, in Section 5, we show that sheaf codes satisfying
certain extendability properties are locally simulatable and we present a toolbox for proving extendability.
In Section 6, we combine the results from Sections 4 and 5 to build perfect zero-knowledge PCPPs
from sheaf codes satisfying both testability and extendability. We also show how to build testable and
extendable sheaf codes from “recursively testable code families”, which we define. Next, we show
that Reed-Solomon codes are a recursively testable code family and use them to instantiate the generic
PZK-PCPP from sheaf codes. We conclude the paper with Section 8, where we build a PCP using
techniques from [BCFGRS17].

In this appendix, we observe that Dinur’s query reduction and gap amplification preserve perfect zero-
knowledge, at the cost of reducing the query bound by a polynomial factor of the query complexity of the
original PCP.
    Dinur [Din07] showed that a PCP of length ℓ with query complexity q can be transformed to a

zero-knowledge with respect to query bound b, then the resulting O(1)-query PCP will have query bound
b/poly(q).
    By the local simulatability lemma [GOS25, Lemma 3.2], it suffices to show that the gap amplification
procedure is poly(q(n))-locally computable from the original PCP. We verify this below, assuming
familiarity with Dinur [Din07].
Lemma A.1. Let (P, V ) be a non-adaptive PZK-PCP system with constnat-size alphabet, polynomial
proof length ℓ(n), query complexity q(n), query bound b(n), polynomial decision complexity, perfect
completeness, and constant soundness error.
   Then, there exist absolute constants c1 , c2 > 0 and a PZK-PCP system (P ′ , V ′ ) with binary alphabet,
proof length ℓ(n) · q(n)c1 , query complexity O(1), query bound b(n)/q(n)c2 , perfect completeness, and
soundness error 1/2.

Sketch of proof. The transformation and the resulting alphabet size, proof length, query complexity,
completeness, and soundness are provided and analysed in [Din07, Theorem 1.5 and Section 8]. It
